summary: In this evidence, recursive self-improvement first appears around 2010 as a theoretical idea from AGI and AI-safety writing: an AI that improves itself in ways that make it better at further improvement, possibly leading to an intelligence explosion or technological singularity. Since about 2023, and especially in 2025-2026, it mostly names practical engineering loops in which LLM agents, harnesses, or models use their own outputs, failures, and experiments to improve themselves, and these loops are measured with benchmarks and governed by safety frameworks.
